chapter: Band family, war years and wrap-up
title: Induction, extensions and being excused
summary: He was sworn in but spared for his service work.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Now, I'm bowling all night, getting tired. I've got to be at the induction center at 6:30 in the morning. I goes down, gets in the line, going through my examination. I got

as far as the eye specialist. Here comes the sargeant up to me. He said, 'Let me see your papers.' He took my papers. He said, 'Follow me.' He brought me to the Major's office and he says sit there. He goes, and about a half hour later, he comes out and gave me a slip. He said, 'Go back to your band.' He said, 'We'll see you when you come back.'

So, I've been doing all this for the service. I don't know if that's got anything to do with it or not. So, I goes back to the band. I'm out there for 8 weeks at this club. At NBC, I was doing recordings, tapes, recordings for overseas. They'd have a guest artist from the movies, like Jack Benny was on my show one time. Marie MacDonald was on another show. You know, every Monday, I had Monday off. And, I was doing that.
So, when I finished that 8 weeks, I figured I go get back to New York. I went back to New York a week. Here come my papers again. Here come my papers again. So, I go on back. I goes down and
this time, I goes all the way through, like, taking the examination. And, they swore me in and everything. I said well, this is it.

And so, therefore, my draft board, we went up there and asked them for a little extension to finish certain dates, to the draft board. And they said, 'How long do you need?' I said about 6 months. Well, they hollered, 'No.' We can't give you that. We can't give you no 6 months. The war will be over by then.'
So, they goes back into another meeting. About an hour later, they came out. They gave me 90 days.

Well, at the end of that 90 days, I was in Boston at the Tick-Tock Club. I got 3 days, and my band, they had booked my band another week. Then, I was supposed to go in the service. I got a wire from my draft board to not to report until you hear from us.
Now, I wondered why that was and someone told me later, through the years. He said well, you had just turned 30 years old and they didn't, one part of that they weren't
taking people at 30. So, they gave you the benefit of the doubt on account of the work you was doing with the Service, and they're saying I was 30. So, I didn't have to go.
